title: Enterprise geofence & failover request evaluation protocol
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Purpose: Establish a repeatable, evidence-based protocol for evaluating enterprise requests that require geographic access controls (geofencing), strict data residency, or custom failover behavior. This ticket codifies intake questions, prioritization rubric, required technical and legal checks, and the routing policy used by PMs/SEs when deciding whether to accept, qualify, or deny a request. Scope: non-bug customer requests from enterprise accounts (SAML/SSO customers, revenue >= $100k ARR) asking for: 1) new region availability, 2) data residency guarantees (data stored/processed exclusively in region), 3) failover routes that deviate from standard Redwood fallbacks, including single-region failback policies. Out of scope: ad-hoc performance benchmarking requests, self-serve hosted API requests from individual dev accounts.
background: We repeatedly get enterprise asks that combine legal residency requirements with availability/failover constraints. Current intake is ad-hoc; decisions sometimes cause rework across infra, legal, and sales. Recent incidents: - Q4 2025: multi-day delay for a carrier requiring all inference logs to remain in-country (result: delayed contract closure). - Q1 2026: manual failover config for a healthcare partner caused inconsistent routing during a regional outage. This protocol should reduce cycle time, clarify who signs trade-offs, and standardize expected engineering effort and cost estimates.
intake_checklist: Customer profile: revenue band, industry (regulated?), contract stage, existing agreements (DPA/SCCs).
Request type: new-region provision | data-residency-only | custom-failover | hybrid.
Data flow map: which artifacts must be kept in-region? (inputs, model weights, logs, metrics, backups).
Traffic shape: expected RPS, avg tokens per request, burst tolerance, SLO requirements.
Security gating: KMS/HSM requirements, encryption at rest in-region, audit log retention duration.
Time horizon: pilot window, production date, runway for compliance and infra changes.
Willingness to pay: committed reserved capacity or cost-plus surcharge?
Risks: single point of failure introduced, cross-region egress charges, support/ops burden.
evaluation_rubric: Priority Score = sum(component scores) where components: Business Impact (0-5), Regulatory Urgency (0-5), Technical Complexity (0-5, inverted), Cost-to-Serve (0-5, inverted), Strategic Alignment (0-5).
Business Impact: revenue upsell likelihood or legal block (5 = contract at risk; 0 = marginal).
Regulatory Urgency: legal/regulator demand for residency (5 = enforcement/penalty likely).
Technical Complexity: 5 = trivial config, 1 = requires infra changes + multi-team rollout. (Invert when computing final priority).
Cost-to-Serve: estimate monthly incremental cost including reserved capacity and egress. High cost reduces priority unless customer funds it.
Thresholds: >=16 -> P0 expedite (dedicated track); 12-15 -> P1 high priority; 8-11 -> P2 schedule; <8 -> P3 / customer-sourced solution recommended.
routing_policy_matrix: If request is data-residency-only AND customer commits to reserved capacity AND Business Impact >=4 -> route to Dedicated-onboarding + Legal for DPA amendment.
If request demands new cloud region but low traffic (<100 RPS) and low regulatory urgency -> suggest edge-proxy with in-country ingress + standard hosted API; label as provisional.
Custom failover deviating from Redwood defaults requires: Eng signoff (runtime+network), SRE runbook, and a canary window with telemetry; otherwise deny.
If customer refuses cost-share for high infra delta -> route to Sales for commercial negotiation and put request into backlog until commit.
decision_log: 2026-02-03: Initial draft protocol presented to PM guild. Feedback: more granularity required for backup retention window (Legal). Action: add explicit log retention matrix.
2026-02-07: Eng provided rough cost model for single-region storage (+10% token cost) and new-region provisioning (2-4 week lead). Action: attach cost ranges to rubric.
2026-02-10: Privacy & Legal reviewed and flagged template DPA amendment as required for all residency commitments. Security review required for KMS in customer VPC.
